hook_text: Two giant rivers meet near a small town. After that, which name does the river keep?
clip_script: Douglas, Northern Cape. From one side, the Vaal, all the way from the Highveld. From the other, the Gariep, all the way from Lesotho. They meet at a confluence, and the Vaal becomes a tributary of the Gariep. A main river and all its tributaries make a river system, like a tree lying on its side. All the land that drains into it is its catchment. And what happens upstream flows down to everyone below.
visual_style: Whiteboard map with two blue rivers flowing together, then a river system branching like a tree, with the catchment shaded around it.
mood: Calm and connected, like seeing how everything links together.
pacing: Two rivers flowing in slowly, a gentle join, then the whole system branching out.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find out which river system your town is in.
